messages:
Nora Li: Proposal: introduce a "Compute Flex Pack" add-on that lets customers commit GPU-equivalent units and choose accelerator mix (A100/H100/ML-TPU) during billing periods. Goal: reduce friction for customers who want flexibility across regions/hardware while preserving our unit economics. Thoughts? :thinking:
Diego Ramos: Interesting. scheduler can map committed units to instance types using conversion factors. we need to lock a conversion table and define preemptible vs reserved behavior. important: perf variability must be surfaced.
Oliver Stone (Finance): We Need a clear conversion matrix and a pricing multiplier. suggested model: base unit = A100-40GB-hour. H100 = 1.6x, TPU-v4 = 1.25x. charge = base rate * multiplier * committed-hours. also need surge/overage policy.
Maya Ortiz: Sales love flexibility but will hate complexity. ask for three canned bundles: Flex-Lite (A100 only), Flex-Mix (allow H100 w/ multiplier), Flex-Premium (guaranteed H100 capacity + priority routing). keep quotes simple.
Samir Gupta (Legal): Contract implications: define "equivalent unit" precisely and list hardware families. include a clause that conversion multipliers are subject to change with 60-day notice and won't affect already invoiced periods. also need SLA wording per hardware class.
Diego Ramos: Implementation checklist: 1) conversion matrix in pricing service, 2) scheduler enhancement to respect commit ratios, 3) telemetry reporting for realized accelerator mix, 4) Console UI to pick bundle. estimate 3 sprints for MVP.
Nora Li: Launch criteria proposed: (A) published conversion matrix + examples, (B) pricing cells/quote templates for 3 bundles, (C) Console UX for selecting mix and viewing estimated avg cost, (D) legal clause + sample contract language.
Oliver Stone (Finance): Also require a TCO example per bundle (1yr/3yr) and sensitivity to utilization. I will run models if Diego gives estimated multipliers and utilization bands (50/70/90%).
Maya Ortiz: For pitches we should present two buyer personas: startups (Flex-Lite, lower commit) and enterprise infra teams (Flex-Premium, multi-region H100). include simple diagrams.
Diego Ramos: Quick conversion draft for discussion:
```
base_unit = A100-40GB-hour
A100-40 = 1.0
H100-80 = 1.6
H100-160 = 3.0
TPU-v4 = 1.25
preemptible_discount = 0.4 (applies after multiplier)
```
This yields straightforward math for invoices.
Samir Gupta (Legal): Draft clause (starter):
```
"Equivalent Unit" means the billing unit derived from the Base Unit conversion table published by Redwood. Redwood may update conversion multipliers with 60 days' notice to Customers; changes will not retroactively alter charged amounts for closed billing periods.
```
I'll add warranty/SLA language.
quote-bot: I can generate sample quote lines once multipliers and base rate are provided.
Nora Li: Next steps: Diego to finalize conversion table + perf caveats by EOD, Oliver to run P&L sims, Maya to request customer-facing bundles, Samir to post legal starter language. We'll reconvene tomorrow to approve pricebook entries. Thanks! :rocket:
